title: Invariant laws remain invariant under n-step kernel powers
source_anchor: Fearnhead–Nemeth–Oates–Sherlock arXiv:2407.12751v1 §1.3, printed pp.17–19 / PDF pp.23–25; Chen–Štefankovič–Vigoda arXiv:2307.13826v4 §3 mixing arguments using ν P^t
target_statement: For any measurable state space, kernel κ and measure μ, if κ.Invariant μ then (κ ^ n).Invariant μ for every n : ℕ; equivalently μ.bind (κ ^ n) = μ.

shared_floor_audit.notes: Exact lower nodes are reused from Mathlib: Kernel.Invariant, Kernel.IsReversible.invariant, the kernel monoid/powers, Chapman–Kolmogorov and Invariant.comp. The missing delta is only closure of invariance under finite powers; no duplicate detailed-balance theorem is introduced.

source_detail_audit.primary_anchor: MCMC §1.3: stationary law is preserved by repeated induction; §1.3.1: detailed balance implies stationarity. Discrete Sampling §3/§3.7 uses ν P^t in mixing bounds.
source_detail_audit.fidelity_boundary: Only finite-step propagation of an already invariant law is formalized. No uniqueness, irreducibility, aperiodicity, convergence from nonstationary starts, spectral gap or mixing rate is inferred.

mcmc_contract.state_space: Arbitrary measurable state space; no topology or density is required.
mcmc_contract.target: A measure μ already invariant for the one-step kernel κ.
mcmc_contract.support: No extra support restriction beyond the well-typed kernel/measure; downstream MH adapters retain their own support/Radon–Nikodym contracts.
mcmc_contract.operator: Discrete-time transition kernel κ and its Mathlib monoid power κ ^ n.
mcmc_contract.clock: One application of κ is one transition; κ ^ n is n transitions.
mcmc_contract.invariance: Exact target invariance is assumed for κ and propagated to κ ^ n.
mcmc_contract.initialization: The law starts exactly at μ; the theorem does not treat another initial distribution.
mcmc_contract.metric: Exact equality of measures; no TV/KL/Wasserstein error bound.
mcmc_contract.cost: Abstract n kernel applications only; no implementation/query cost theorem.
mcmc_contract.objective: Propagate a stationary law through a finite number of MCMC transitions, not estimate a mixing time or expectation error.
mcmc_contract.source_proof_status: The MCMC primary explicitly states repeated stationarity; the Lean proof reduces it to Mathlib's invariant-composition API.
mcmc_contract.periodicity: Not required for this theorem: a periodic chain may still preserve a stationary law. Periodicity or laziness becomes relevant only for convergence/mixing claims, which are explicitly outside this cell.

discrete_state_contract.state_space: Shared theorem is state-neutral; the Discrete Sampling consumer specializes to a finite configuration type.
discrete_state_contract.support: No additional support condition at this shared layer; finite Gibbs adapters specify feasible configurations and positive-probability conditioning events.
discrete_state_contract.target: An invariant measure μ; finite applications may instantiate a Gibbs law.
discrete_state_contract.operator: Markov transition kernel κ and n-step kernel κ ^ n.
discrete_state_contract.clock: One κ application is one update in the downstream model's declared clock; no sweep/per-site conversion is made here.
discrete_state_contract.reversibility: Not required. Reversibility is an upstream sufficient condition for invariance via Mathlib Kernel.IsReversible.invariant.
discrete_state_contract.pinning: Not applicable to the shared theorem itself; each pinned Gibbs law is a separate downstream instantiation.
discrete_state_contract.regime: All n : ℕ and every kernel/measure satisfying exact one-step invariance.
discrete_state_contract.metric: Exact measure equality; no mixing discrepancy.
discrete_state_contract.cost: No model-specific update or sweep complexity claim.
discrete_state_contract.source_proof_status: The discrete textbook uses P^t for the evolved law; this cell supplies only the stationary special case.
discrete_state_contract.aperiodicity_or_absolute_gap: Not required because this theorem makes no convergence or spectral-gap claim.
